evidence.note: Writer resolves the store with git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir through deps.Exec, which RealDeps wires to gate.RealExec (GIT_* scrubbed)
Reader StoreDir runs the same rev-parse through the same scrubbed gate.RealExec; StoreDirIn is the single layout definition, also used by session bindings
Store, Sidecar (CommonDir: true) and Terminal all take the common dir, so audit, sidecars and ledger agree on <common>/metareview
Migration ordering: roots() moves runs, then copies ledger rows passing the collision list, before any Store/Exists/peek call in init, openRun and diff

Rows of collided runs are skipped and set deferred, which suppresses the size stamp so the row follows once the collision is resolved; appendRow dedupes under flock so concurrent unlocked row migration cannot duplicate
TestMigrateLegacyRowsSkipsCollidedRuns pins both the skip and the no-stamp behaviour; targeted migrate/legacy/store/abandoned tests pass in record, run, cli, status, repo
record-lenses --from-run reads the common-dir store first and falls back only to the single 0.13.x main-checkout location with a warning, matching writer and migration

Abandoned-run scan reads legacy then store (rename-safe ordering, dedup by id) and attributes via enterable-ancestor toplevel within the same common dir; docs (ARCHITECTURE, USAGE, skills/status) describe this scoping accurately
Docs claim git >= 2.31 for --path-format=absolute; MinGitVersion is 2.31, consistent

findings.note: A ledger-row conflict (legacy fsm row whose id the common ledger holds for a different head/workflow) is reported as STORE_COLLISION only on the first pass: conflicts do not set deferred, so the size stamp is written and later fsm commands skip the legacy ledger and never repeat the warning, whereas run-directory collisions are re-reported on every command. Harmless (nothing is lost or merged), but the operator sees the row conflict once.

evidence.note: stamp written whenever no collided row was deferred
